transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-08-02 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Alex Reed (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Jordan Li (Redwood Solutions Eng - joined late), Samir Patel (OrthoQuest CTO), Lina Gomez (CISO), Evan Park (Cloud Architect), Tara Nguyen (Legal)
Shared artifacts: redwood-security-pack.pdf (link), private-deploy-checklist.xlsx, benchmark-spreadsheet.csv (shared in chat)

Summary (auto): first intake to map compliance gates and hosting preferences. Customer leaning private with VPC but wants fallback to Dedicated in prod. Key topics: SOC 2 scope, ISO 27001, SAML SSO, RBAC model, audit logging, KMS/HSM integration, data retention and purging, network egress.

Topics: 1) Compliance and certs 2) Identity & access 3) Encryption & key mgmt 4) Audit logs & retention 5) Deployment topology options

Transcript:
00:00 Alex Reed: hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time, uh this is Alex from Redwood, AE, with Maya who's our solutions engineer, Jordan will pop in a bit later. quick intro round?
00:12 Samir Patel: yeah hi i'm Samir, CTO at OrthoQuest, we do device-integrated scheduling and patient follow-ups, we're evaluating inference platforms for clinical triage models.
00:20 Lina Gomez: lina, CISO, i'll flag security and legal needs, will be quick.
00:24 Evan Park: evan, cloud architect, i'll own the network and infra bits.
00:28 Tara Nguyen: tara from legal, privacy and retention questions.
00:31 Maya Chen: great thanks, quick agenda; compliance scope (soc two / iso), identity and auth, encryption and kms, logs/retention, and deployment options: hosted/dedicated/private. sound good?
01:02 Samir Patel: yes sounds good. we, um, at a high level we want to keep PHI inside our VPC, so privacy regs are the driver. we currently use EKS on AWS, HashiV... Hashi VN Vault for secrets and AWS KMS.
01:25 Lina Gomez: to be explicit we need SOC 2 type II and ISO 27001 controls in place for vendor risk. also SAML SSO with our Okta instance, and role-based access with least privilege. audit logs must be immutable for at least 7 years for some workflows, and 3 years is typical otherwise.
01:46 Alex Reed: okay that's great context. quick note on certifications: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certs for our control plane - i'll attach the certs after the call. for private deployments we can run a customer-controlled control plane inside your VPC and still enable the same agent sidecar for inference nodes.
02:05 Samir: can you clarify what you mean by control plane? like we want all PHI to stay on-prem/VPC and not go through any shared planes.
02:15 Maya Chen: yeah good question. for Redwood Private we ship a private control plane that you host in your account — the control plane handles orchestration and metrics but it can be configured so no raw payloads leave your VPC. the inference nodes live inside your subnets. there is a small outbound for telemetry and heartbeat by default but that can be configured to use your proxy or blocked; we also have an air-gapped on-prem bundle. sometimes the transcript shows 'control plane' as redwood-managed but for private it's customer-managed.
03:00 Evan Park: what's the story on keys — we use AWS KMS and an HSM-backed key policy for encrypting PHI at rest, can Redwood integrate?
03:10 Maya Chen: yes we support external KMS via customer CMKs with AWS KMS, and HSM-backed CloudHSM if you need dedicated HSMs. for dedicated and private deployments we can be configured to use a customer-managed KMS key so we never hold the plaintext. for hosted API we by default use our managed KMS but can discuss customer key options for enterprise.
03:36 Lina Gomez: what's the audit trail look like — we need immutable logs and chain-of-custody for access to keys and model requests. where do logs go?
03:45 Maya Chen: audit logs can be exported to your logging sink — S3, CloudWatch, or a 3rd party like Splunk. for private deployments logs live in your account. we provide structured request logs that include request id, model used, token counts, redaction flags. note sometimes our transcriptions call it K V cache instead of KV cache, ignore that.
04:20 Alex Reed: quick interjection on retention: we have configurable retention for logs and artifacts; common patterns are 90 days for raw request payloads, 3 years for access logs, 7 years for certain regulated records. Tara, is there a minimum you need?
04:35 Tara Nguyen: for device/clinical traces we may need 7 years for audit. for other less-sensitive telemetry 1-3 years. also need data deletion proof for records older than retention windows.
05:00 Samir Patel: and is that deletion provable? we sometimes need attestations for data purges.
05:07 Maya Chen: yes we can provide deletion APIs and purge job logs; for private deployments you run the purge in your account. for hosted we provide workflows and audit records showing deletion activity. we'll put together a sample purge runbook.
05:30 Evan Park: network concerns: firewall egress rules, we use restrictive NAT. will Redwood need wide egress to external repos?
05:38 Maya Chen: for private you can lock egress; the nodes need access to your internal model artifacts store or our image repo if you opt in; we can mirror images into your registry. also for model updates we support offline bundles if your environment is hermetic.
06:05 Samir Patel: great. what about identity — SSO/SAML and RBAC? our compliance team mandates single sign-on via Okta and SCIM provisioning, and granular admin roles.
06:17 Maya Chen: we support SAML 2.0, Okta, Azure AD, plus SCIM for provisioning. RBAC is role-based with customizable roles — you can map Okta groups to Redwood roles, and for private deployments the SAML assertion can be validated by your IdP without Redwood ever seeing raw credentials.
06:45 Lina Gomez: can we get audit logs for admin role changes, key rotations, and who pulled model snapshots?
06:52 Maya Chen: yep all admin actions are logged; key rotation events are included. model pulls are recorded with IP and identity where available. retention and immutability can be set in the sink.
07:20 Alex Reed: question from my side — are you evaluating Dedicated (reserved) vs Private fully? any constraints on timing or budget?
07:28 Samir Patel: ideal timeline is pilot in Q4, production late Q1, budget likely to be a committed monthly for Dedicated or a on-prem capital for Private; security is the gating item.
07:38 Alex Reed: understood. we'll layout cost tradeoffs in the follow-up.
07:46 Evan Park: encryption in transit? do you support mTLS between control plane and nodes?
07:50 Maya Chen: yes mTLS for node-control comms, TLS 1.3 for API endpoints; mutual TLS is enforced in private/dedicated modes. sometimes the transcript garbles the cert type to just 'm T L S' — but yes it's mutual TLS.
08:10 Lina Gomez: KMS policies — we need separation of duty for key admins vs operations. can Redwood support key usage policies that only allow decryption by certain roles?
08:20 Maya Chen: absolutely, with customer CMKs you can define IAM policies and Redwood's service principal only has encrypt/decrypt as scoped by your policy; we can document the minimal permissions.
08:33 Tara Nguyen: from legal side, we need data processing agreement (DPA) language for PHI, and proof of subprocessors.
08:40 Alex Reed: we'll send draft DPA and list of subprocessors. for Private, there are fewer subprocessors since most infra lives in your account.
09:05 Samir Patel: how do you handle model weights — are they considered customer data or vendor IP? we want model weights to be treated as artifacts with access controls.
09:14 Maya Chen: model weights are customer artifacts in Private and Dedicated if you bring your own or we store them in your registry. in Hosted we host model artifacts but we can enable per-customer isolation and provide encrypted storage and access logs.
09:40 Evan Park: retention of request payloads, is there a way to redact PII automatically before logs land in S3?
09:48 Maya Chen: we have pre-ingest redaction plugins and a redaction config: PII scrubbing can be enabled; it's not perfect but works for common patterns. we'll share the list of patterns and the caveats.
10:05 Samir Patel: do you support legal hold? for e-discovery we may need to suspend deletion for certain records.
10:12 Maya Chen: yes a legal hold flag can prevent purges for specific request ids; for Private you control that workflow.
10:25 Jordan Li (joined): hey sorry late; quick question on performance vs encryption — do you see any perf impact with HSM-backed keys?
10:34 Maya Chen: small crypto overhead on key ops but for token-level inference it's negligible; we often cache DEKs (data encryption keys) locally with K-V cache so we don't call KMS per token. sometimes notes transcribe 'K V cache' as 'K V Kash' — ignore that.
11:00 Lina Gomez: any third-party pen test results? we need an executive summary of recent red team engagements.
11:06 Alex Reed: yes we'll attach the latest pentest exec summary and remediation notes.
11:15 Tara Nguyen: regarding certifications, want the audit period and scope — e.g., what systems were in scope for SOC 2?
11:22 Alex Reed: good call, we'll include the scope doc. also note that for Private deployments the SOC scope is different since you're operating the control plane; we'll annotate which controls remain Redwood's responsibility.
12:00 Samir Patel: ok, on network egress again — if we block outbound entirely, can you do a full air-gap bundle including models and images via an offline transfer?
12:09 Maya Chen: yes we support air-gapped installs; it adds some ops work but it's a supported flow.
12:25 Evan Park: concerning monitoring and tracing, can we integrate with our existing X-Ray/Datadog stacks?
12:32 Maya Chen: yes metrics and traces can be exported; traces will include request spans, model inference durations, and latency breakdowns. PII should not be in traces, we'll scrub any payload fragments.
13:05 Samir Patel: any required agent-level permissions for nodes? we prefer least privilege.
13:11 Maya Chen: minimal kube roles for node lifecycle and secrets read for model artifacts; we can provide a helm chart with RBAC templates.
13:35 Tara Nguyen: retention - one more time: 7 years for certain audit trails, 3 years for access logs, 90 days for payloads unless flagged for retention. also need proof-of-deletion and chain-of-custody.
13:50 Alex Reed: noted. we'll deliver a suggested retention matrix in follow-up.
14:05 Maya Chen: next steps from our side — i'll produce the VPC/private deployment checklist, KMS integration guide, and sample SCIM/SAML mappings. alex will send certs and DPA. jordan will coordinate pen-test summary.
14:30 Samir Patel: from OrthoQuest, we'll send our retention policy doc and the list of systems that must not leave the VPC.
14:45 Tara Nguyen: legal will review DPA and return comments.
15:00 Alex Reed: great, recap and timeline then: alex sends certs + DPA by EOD 2026-08-02, maya posts deployment checklist and KMS notes by 2026-08-09, schedule technical deep dive for week of 2026-08-10. samir to provide retention policy by 2026-08-06. sound accurate?
15:22 Samir Patel: sounds good.
15:26 Lina Gomez: yes.
15:30 Alex Reed: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links.
15:35 Meeting end

Questions raised:

End of transcript.
